name: Nemotron 3.5 Parse
purpose: Turn page images into structured text with semantic layout classes, bounding boxes, reading order, tables and chart data; small and fast for high page throughput (card).

license.name: OpenMDW-1.1 (tokenizer MIT)
license.notes: LICENSE read: permission to deal in the model materials without restriction; when distributing keep the agreement and origin notices; patent/copyright suit against anyone over the materials ends the grant; no restrictions on outputs.

architecture.kind: encoder-decoder VLM: C-RADIOv4-SO400M vision encoder (439M) plus 10-layer mBART causal visual-prefix decoder (191.8M)
architecture.attention: GQA decoder, 16 query / 8 KV heads; dynamic rectangular NaViT preprocessing
architecture.drafter: bundled one-step MTP head plus optional 89.3M DFlash2 drafter in dflash2/
architecture.why_this_design: not stated beyond small size and high throughput; the card describes the parts (1D-conv adapter compressing the vision sequence, content-normalized coordinates)

variants.notes: plus dflash2 drafter 0.18 GB; custom code (trust_remote_code)

pc-12gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a VRAM budget of 9.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-16gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a VRAM budget of 13.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-24gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a VRAM budget of 21.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

pc-32gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a VRAM budget of 29.6 GB (VRAM minus about 2.4 GB), KV cache not included

mac-16-24gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a GPU share of about 12 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-32gb.notes: 2.7 GB against a GPU share of about 22 GB (KV cache not included)

mac-64gb+.notes: 2.7 GB against a GPU share of about 52 GB (KV cache not included)

other: vLLM with native Parse and DFlash2 plugin
engine_support.notes: llama.cpp support not mentioned on the card.

benchmarks.name: ParseBench tables / charts / faithfulness / formatting / grounding
throughput on one H200, BF16, DFlash2
olmOCR-bench / OmniDocBench v1.6
benchmarks.variant: as listed in another vendor's comparison table

strengths: highest ParseBench score in NVIDIA's own comparison, above LightOnOCR-3-4B 75.10 and 0.8B 74.60
very fast: 13 to 19 pages/s on one H200
tables 84.67 and layout boxes with classes
weaknesses: third-party tables put it well behind on olmOCR-bench (62.7) and OmniDocBench v1.6 (80.13), so the lead is specific to ParseBench
MOSCAR measures only simple synthetic renderings
best_for: high-volume page parsing with boxes and table HTML
soft.maturity: NVIDIA Nemotron line; 27k downloads; derivatives already exist (OpenThai2.1)

tona_fit.reason: 0.6B, most permissive licence of the parsers (OpenMDW), strong on ParseBench tables and charts, built for throughput. The wide gap between ParseBench (leader) and olmOCR/OmniDocBench (behind the field) means the lead is benchmark-dependent; compare on our own German documents before offering it.
blockers: custom encoder-decoder architecture without a Tona or llama.cpp module

open_questions: ParseBench numbers by a third party
why olmOCR-bench and OmniDocBench results trail the ParseBench lead
